strengths: MSAM offers a useful, simple efficiency improvement: reusing momentum eliminates SAM’s additional forward/backward pass. The reported relative speeds of 0.99 for MSAM and 0.52 for SAM support the practical motivation.

The experiments show consistent improvements over base optimizers across CNNs and ViTs. On CIFAR100, WRN-16-4 improves from 76.90% to 79.11%, approaching SAM’s 79.25%. Equal-compute comparisons and compatibility with adaptive and BatchNorm-only perturbations strengthen the empirical contribution.

Extensive ablations examine perturbation sign, alternative directions, normalization, learning rate, and momentum. The finding that decoupling perturbation strength from the learning-rate schedule matters more than normalization provides useful insight into the relationship with NAG.

The presentation generally explains the algorithm clearly and situates it within relevant prior work. Hyperparameter scans and a public code link support reproducibility, while instability and the imperfect relationship between sharpness and generalization are discussed candidly.
weaknesses: The theoretical guarantee is not established as stated. Proposition 1 fails for negative Hessian trace: with H = -I, its left side is -E[1{||epsilon|| <= rho}||epsilon||²], which is strictly greater than the claimed upper bound -rho². Theorem 3 also omits necessary loss, smoothness, and population-loss assumptions when invoking the SAM proof. Moreover, minibatch slope measurements do not establish the full-training-loss condition in Setting 1.

The ImageNet comparison uses unequal perturbation schedules despite evidence that this materially affects results. Appendix A.3 disables MSAM during warm-up but keeps SAM active; disabling SAM during warm-up improves its accuracy from 69.2% to 69.8%, versus MSAM’s 69.1%. Matched scheduling is needed to substantiate the claimed parity.

Evaluation uncertainty and model selection are insufficiently controlled. Appendix A.6 reports the best perturbation strengths alongside test-accuracy sweeps without describing an independent selection split. Most ImageNet results use one seed, and uncertainty estimated from small baseline models cannot establish variability for other models or optimizers.

Claims of broadly comparable SAM accuracy need qualification. MSAM trails SAM by 2.4 percentage points on ViT-S/16 at 300 epochs and 2.0 points on ViT-B/16 at 90 epochs. ImageNet evidence at equal compute is limited to ViT-S/32, leaving the tradeoff on these harder cases unresolved.

The mechanistic evidence remains limited: alignment after projection into a two-dimensional plane can conceal large orthogonal gradient differences, and selected directional curvatures do not establish global sharpness minimization. Reproducibility also needs explicit AdamW update details, zero-momentum initialization handling, and hardware-specific absolute timings. Together with the theoretical and evaluation gaps, these shortcomings outweigh the promising practical results.
